clauses.reason: Terminated by its own terms, as amended. The original operative sentence exempted Edwards for "a period of one year ending October 31, 1941". EO 8844 of 1941-08-08, before that day, amended the order so that it exempts him for "a period of one year ending October 31, 1942" (the amending sentence reads "is hereby amended so as to exempt Mr. Edwards from compulsory retirement for a period of one year ending October 31, 1942"). Clause text before the amendment: "a period of one year ending October 31, 1941"; after: "a period of one year ending October 31, 1942"; the amendment changes the substance of the period by one year. The first end is recorded as 1942-10-31, inclusive (the exemption runs through that day, per the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on stated end dates); the exclusive reading, under which the exemption ends when that day begins, is the alternative. The amendment is a later event with its own date and quote, not an end (owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on strike-and-insert amendments). The earlier orders recited in the text (EO 8259, EO 8525) are earlier instruments and do not bear on this end. No later order, statute or regulation held in the packet changes the period further; see the order-level checks.

research_rationale:
Text and identity: read in full in the registered American Presidency Project transcription (jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts/executive-order-8827-exemption-harry-t-edwards-from-compulsory-retirement-for-age.txt; grade mirror_transcription, acceptable_as_original false; standing note: original not yet held; replace and re-check quotes when an official copy is retrieved). Page check per jobs/claim-kit/AGENT_PROTOCOL.md (working-text paragraph), done 2026-11-04: the APP mirror page record with the same sha256 in jobs/app-executive-orders/output/MIRROR_DOCUMENTS.jsonl (Common Crawl capture 2025-06-17T21:44:22Z) has the heading "Executive Order 8827—Exemption of Harry T. Edwards From Compulsory Retirement for Age", its date (1941-07-24) and subject agree with the held text, and its text_sha256 equals the held file's. Identity: the register lists this number with date 1941-07-24, signer Franklin D. Roosevelt and the title "Exemption of Harry T. Edwards From Compulsory Retirement for Age"; the held text concerns Harry T. Edwards and ends with the signature "FRANKLIN D ROOSEVELT" and the date line "July 24, 1941.". Clauses are quoted from that registered file, not from the unregistered clause-drafts copy.
Content: the order has one recital and one operative sentence. It further exempts one named employee, Harry T. Edwards (senior technologist, Bureau of Plant Industry, Department of Agriculture), from compulsory retirement for age under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (U.S.C., title 5, sec. 715a), for a period of one year ending October 31, 1941. The recital says he "was exempted from compulsory retirement for age for periods totaling two years by Executive Orders No. 8259 of September 21, 1939, and No. 8525 of August 26, 1940" and asks that he "be further exempted from such compulsory retirement for a period of one year"; those earlier orders (EO 8259 and EO 8525) are earlier instruments, not later events and not ends of this order. The inventory is one clause, the exemption.
Later event and reading: EO 8844 of August 8, 1941 (read in full in its registered APP text, jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts/executive-order-8844-amending-executive-order-no-8827-july-24-1941-exempting-harry-t.txt; its own claim is in this packet) cites this order as "Executive Order No. 8827 of July 24, 1941, exempting Harry T. Edwards" and provides that this order is amended; the held sentence reads "is hereby amended so as to exempt Mr. Edwards from compulsory retirement for a period of one year ending October 31, 1942". EO 8844 was signed on 1941-08-08, before the original last day (October 31, 1941), so the clause was still running when its period was changed. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on strike-and-insert amendments, the clause continues, amended, and the amendment is a later event that records the clause text before and after: before, "a period of one year ending October 31, 1941"; after, "a period of one year ending October 31, 1942". The amendment changes the last day by one year, so the substance of the period changed. The first end is therefore the amended last day, October 31, 1942, not the original October 31, 1941. EO 8844 states no separate effective date, so the amendment is recorded as effective on its date of signing, 1941-08-08.
